pages.text: "Straw pile! I'll jump right in!" Little brother Mumu hopped outside the mill door. Across the yard, yellow straw piled like a mountain. A cart path lay between, running from the bridge to the mill door.
Looking only at straw, not the cart path, Mumu ran out. "Mumu, wait!" Dad caught him firmly with a wing. His feet slid forward as he wobbled to a stop.
Rattle, rattle! A cart loaded with wheat sacks rolled from the bridge. Their neighbor Mr. Goat pulled it right past Mumu's nose. Mumu's heart thumped. Both webbed feet stayed planted.
Dad crouched, meeting Mumu's eyes. "Don't just cross a cart path. I'll show you how." Mumu nodded his neck up and down. "Yes! Teach me!"
Mr. Goat stopped the cart and looked back. "Wheat sacks are heavy, so a cart can't stop quickly. You need to look first." Mumu watched its wheels quietly. They really were big.

Dad and Mr. Goat called together, "One, stop before the cart path! Two, raise your wings high! Three, look both ways, hold Dad's wing, and cross!" Mumu raised both wings. "Stop, look for carts, cross!"
Mr. Goat's cart went all the way inside the mill. Mumu stopped before the path. Wings high! Look this way, look that way. "Stop, look for carts, cross!"
Mumu plunged into the straw! Straw fluttered. "I remembered the promises myself!" One tail flick. By the door, Dad clapped his wings. Mr. Goat stamped his front feet too.

Now Mumu always stopped at the cart path. "One, stop before the path! Two, wings high! Three, look both ways, hold Dad's wing, and cross!" Coming back, Mumu called first too. "Stop, look for carts, cross!"

Dad wrapped Mumu against his chest in both wings. "You stopped right before the cart!" Even in a hurry, promises come first when crossing the cart path. Inside Dad's wings, Mumu called, "Stop, look for carts, cross!"
